quest.title: Base Note: Auguste
quest.description: The true identity of "Kirya" has finally been exposed... His path of vengeance reaching its end.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Primogem x60, Mora x44000, Guide to Order x5, "Yelena" x1, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Pomum de Ambra Chapter: Act I
chapter.title: Floral Debt, Blood Due

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: *panting*... *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The scent... getting stronger... almost at the...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...Did they catch up that fast?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: No... my strength is just waning...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...But, it doesn't matter... This is far enough.

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Ahh!

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: This is... A garden of Auguste flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...But, it's not mine... It's the one that was set on fire all those years ago in Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...Yelena?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Yelena!

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: You tried to hide it from me, but I... I always understood!

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: The reason why you continued to use the Delusion... The reason why you set your garden on fire... It was all because of me!

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...I shouldn't have listened to you that day. I shouldn't have taken the Mora and ran...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: But, by the time I realized something wasn't right... there was nothing left. The flowers were gone... and so were you...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...I know I'm almost twenty years too late... I should have come looking for you earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: I should have... I should have died with you that day...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...Yelena?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Yelena!?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: No... Don't leave me... Please...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Yelena!

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: ...Emilie?

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: I... I'm alive? No, that's not possible. I saw her... Yelena... We were together...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...No. That was an illusion, likely brought about by the residual toxin in your body coupled with the pollen in the air, neither of which are fatal.

dialogues.speaker: Kirya
dialogues.text: No, the amount of "Auguste" I drank... It should've been enough...

choices.text: I'm sorry to say this, but...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: ...A fake? But, how...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...We started making the preparations last night with one goal in mind.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...To create a perfect accord.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: ...So, you switched the bottles of "Auguste" and then lied to me about Sylvain's death...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Convincing you that your revenge had been completed... was the easiest way to get you to let down your guard.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Impossible... even if you found a way to switch out the bottles, there's no way you could have made an accord!

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: If "Auguste" was so easy to replicate, Yelena wouldn't have...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: It was a combination of Rainbow Roses, Glaze Lilies, and Cecilias... Those ingredients would have conflicted with each other if you tried to combine them in the past.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But recently, we found a way for them to work together.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: ...Rainbow Roses... Glaze Lilies... and Cecilias?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ..."Auguste" was created over ten years ago. All this time, people never stopped analyzing it, never stopped trying to recreate it.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Perfumery techniques are advancing day by day. We've found better ways to extract essential oils, separate oils and fats... we even discovered new ways to combine fragrances together.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: The mythos surrounding "Auguste" may have been untouchable almost twenty years ago... But, now, it's time for it to become a thing of the past.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: The past...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: You've been working as a perfumer for all these years... You should have always known that it is possible to make an accord, even if only in theory.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But, the meaning you assigned to "Auguste" became so inflated, you allowed yourself to get lost in it... just like the "Perfume Mania" that captivated the public all those years ago.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: You believed in its "divinity" and "grandeur"... You believed it was entirely "one of a kind."

choices.text: And, in the process, you forgot...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Your obsession with "Auguste" is also what allowed us to predict how you intended your plan to end... and to make preparations in advance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We just didn't expect it to happen so fast...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Or that you would activate the Delusion.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Ha... Haha...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Well... you hit the nail on the head, now didn't you?

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: So... Sylvain isn't dead...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Since you've been preparing your accord since last night... I assume you've also figured out my method, then?

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: That means the news of Sylvain's death, the crowd gathered outside the hotel this morning... It was all an act you put on with the Sheriff?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Yes. If we hadn't, you might have resorted to the Delusion out of desperation, or continued to use your "Spirit Borneol" and "Auguste" combination to wreak havoc...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Who knows... Maybe I would have just offed myself then and there.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I know if you had things your way, you would carry the truth of "Edgar's" demise and the secrets of this garden to the grave, but I'm sorry, Master... I don't want to see any more death.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Sylvain only inhaled a small amount of poison. He's being detained as we speak.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: All the crimes he concealed back then will be exposed in a court of law for everyone to see, and all his secrets will be revealed... The same goes for you as well.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Is that so... Well, I suppose I'll be spending the rest of my days in a prison cell, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah... He accepted that kinda fast...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: ...I don't feel the need to justify my actions, nor do I intend to repent for them.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: I did what I set out to do. I may have lost in the end, but it was my choice every step of the way. And if I could do it all over again...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Hah... But, there's no going back, is there?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Be careful, everyone. This environment is dangerous, I'll lead the way...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: ...Stick close... We can't let Edgar die...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Looks like I'm almost out of time... Although, I do have one final question, Emilie.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Of course, Master.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: The combination you used to make your accord... How did you figure it out?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...The scent of "Auguste" is complex and varied, yet the main ingredient consists of a single variety of flower.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: So, as I was analyzing the sample yesterday, I got to thinking... What if the scent of the Auguste flower was already imbued with that complexity during its cultivation?

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: You're saying... Yelena designed "Auguste" to have the scent of multiple flowers?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Rainbow Roses, Glaze Lilies, Cecilias... The perfumers of the past knew that if you combined their essential oils directly, they would just cancel each other out. It was a conundrum they could never solve.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But, if you cultivate a new flower species that intrinsically carries the unique features of those three scents, you can bypass that issue entirely... It goes without saying, that for the time, this idea was a stroke of genius.

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: Rainbow Roses, Glaze Lilies, and Cecilias... Hah, those really do seem like flowers you would choose...

response.speaker: Kirya
response.text: ...Yelena.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Not long after that, the Eremites rush over...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Kirya accepts his fate without saying a word.

choices.text: That it was a bottle of perfume, nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: G—Ghost! It's a ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's alright, please calm down and take a deep breath... Can you tell us what you saw?

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: *panting* I saw a black shadow... It ran right past me...

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: How could... How could something like that happen in broad daylight...

dialogues.speaker: Babak
dialogues.text: A shadow-like figure with an ominous aura?

dialogues.speaker: Babak
dialogues.text: Sorry, I didn't see anything. I was busy taking inventory...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh*... If we go any further, we'll be out of Port Ormos! They'll be hardly any witnesses...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's alright. I can detect a faint whiff of the scent from here. I would say he passed by this location not too long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Hm, it's this way. Please, follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: From today until the end of the exhibition, the hotel and surrounding buildings have been temporarily rented out by the exhibitor, and are not accepting outside guests at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience.

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: Ah! Oguz!

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: Are you alright? W—Were you attacked?

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: Argh... No, no... I'm alright. I was just chasing after that figure, and then, all of a sudden, I didn't feel so hot...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Let me take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The air definitely feels heavy... It smells nice, but for some reason, it's hard to breathe...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: This feeling... I've encountered it before...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Everything looks alright. It was probably just the stress of the chase combined with the impact of the environment. A bit of rest would do you some good.

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: I can't rest! Mr. Edgar is still in there! He taught my sister how to make perfume...

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: He's a good man... I can't just abandon him to die by Kirya's hand!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Oguz... You need to calm down and listen to me. Edgar is the one we're after. He and Kirya are the same person.

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: But... How is that possible!? I thought you said Kirya was in his thirties?

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: Mr. Edgar is seventy something... Changing your appearance to look decades older... That doesn't seem possible!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's precisely why he had to resort to extraordinary measures to age himself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...A Delusion.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Kirya used a Delusion to bring back the Auguste flower, corroding his body in the process... just like his older sister.

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: No... He couldn't have. Mr. Edgar has been in Port Ormos for years! If someone started impersonating him all of a sudden, we would have noticed!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: And what if the impersonation started before he ever set foot in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...I've yet to confirm it, but I suspect Kirya killed the real Edgar in Fontaine not long after his release from prison.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: While Edgar was incarcerated, Kirya started making preparations to replace him, including forcefully aging his body, studying perfumery... and planning the real Edgar's demise.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The new "Edgar" then decided to relocate to Sumeru, seemingly out of an innocuous desire to let go of the past. He even left perfume-making in favor of mentoring students... But, these decisions were all for a specific purpose... the need to distance himself from anyone who might see through the facade.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: And Sumeru fit the bill to a tee. With no one around to question his identity, all he had to do was grow a beard, don a pair of glasses, make a few minor alterations to his appearance... and everyone would believe he was exactly who he claimed — Edgar, a perfumer from Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: As the years went by, he removed his disguise little by little and continued to refine his skills... It would have been a gradual process, one that ensured no one around him would notice anything unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That explains why Sylvain said he barely recognized Edgar back at the hotel...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He aged himself decades beyond his years just so he could accomplish his revenge... Is that even worth it?

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: I... I need to find Mr. Edgar... He's not that kind of person, he can't be... *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: What you really need is to get out of here and rest!

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: No, I... I can keep going!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wait... This environment is likely being influenced by the Delusion. Any discomfort, no matter how slight, should not be treated lightly.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I know how to relieve your symptoms, Mr. Oguz... Please, come with me and rest.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm sure Kirya... No, Edgar wouldn't want any more innocent people implicated in all this.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: #Collei's right. {NICKNAME} and I will take things from here. From our brief exposure to "Auguste," it would seem the substance has little effect on us...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: This leads me to believe those blessed with a Vision or capable of wielding elemental power are more resistant to the effects of abnormal elemental energy. In other words, this environment doesn't pose as much of a risk to us.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Actually, now that I think about it, this stronghold likely has multiple points of entry. If the target were to escape from a different point of entry, that might allow him to evade capture...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...I hate to trouble you, but we need people to survey the perimeter...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Heh... Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...Hear that? We're heading out! There's work to be done! Oguz, head back to Port Ormos and start gathering reinforcements!

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: Got it...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Emilie, Paimon... Please, be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: For someone whose only purpose in life is revenge, there's no telling what they'll do when there's no reason to move forward.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Don't worry. This isn't the end, not for us... or for Kirya.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...We're not going to let "Auguste" kill anyone else. It's time for the mythos to fade into obscurity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah... Look at all the Auguste flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many of them... Paimon can't believe a single person did all this! It must've taken a lot of time...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I fear that statement is truer than you know, Paimon. Using a Delusion comes at a cost... not just time, but the time you have left to live...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, why would Kirya need this many Auguste flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He only needed a few bottles of "Auguste" to carry out his plan, right?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Perhaps hatred wasn't the only emotion fueling his obsession with "Auguste."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Not long ago, he told me he didn't want all the flowers transported to Sumeru to wither away in a foreign land.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, Kirya betrayed Snezhnaya, abandoned Fontaine, and lived his entire life in Sumeru under the guise of someone else...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: For someone with nowhere to call home... Perhaps dying among a bed of Auguste flowers, just like his sister, is the best homecoming he could ask for.

talks.objective: Go to the secret garden's entrance
Keep your appointment on the 2nd floor of the Hotel Debord

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: ...Did you know? Miss Emilie's releasing a new perfume!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: Ah, right! I heard about that! I think it's called... "Yelena"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Seems like everyone in Fontaine is talking about the new perfume you're releasing!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I was hoping to release it without such a fuss, but... the news spread way faster than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I just hope it won't become the source of some new "myth"... especially after all the work we did to demystify "Auguste."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I did! Although, I made a few modifications to the formula to make the scent more pleasant and long-lasting... I actually brought a few samples with me today. I hope they're to your liking.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Also... I was hoping you could try out the fragrance before I officially release it, and tell me your thoughts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! A good sense of taste and sense of smell go hand in hand, you know. Just leave it to Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...*sniff* Ooh, it smells great!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not sure that's the kind of feedback she had in mind...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Haha, it's alright. All feedback is worth considering.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Besides, when it comes to perfume... commenting on whether it smells good is the most straightforward assessment you can ask for. There doesn't always have to be a deeper meaning.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Speaking of deeper meanings... Kirya's final question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right... Do those flowers have some special meaning? Hearing their names seemed to have an effect on him...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Hm, if I had to guess... I'd say it probably has something to do with the language of flowers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The language of flowers? Oh, we've heard of that before. Paimon remembers hearing something like... the "Cecilia" represents "the true feelings of the prodigal son"...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: What each flower is said to represent varies by person and across different moments in history... the same is true for the flowers that make up the scent of Auguste.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: After returning to Fontaine, I did some research... and it turns out, the meanings of those three flowers can be reassembled to form a single phrase...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "...Forget the past, and keep on living."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Perhaps that's the legacy Yelena always intended, not the nobility and grandeur most people associate with Auguste.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Or maybe... That's what she hoped for her brother...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think Kirya knew about that?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I paid him a visit before his trial and explained what I found... But, he didn't seem to care.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "Who knows? Maybe she didn't mean anything by it at all?" — that was his response.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "...Yelena is gone. We'll never know what she was thinking. We can look for meaning all we want, but it'll never be anything but conjecture."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "Even if that is what she was trying to say, I would never be able to forget her."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "...Avenging her death... That was the meaning I chose for my life."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Kirya cultivated his revenge like a flower. He was commited to making it bloom, even if, in the end, it didn't bear the fruit he was hoping for...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Kirya.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: In any case, he did want me to pass along his thanks.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "...Thank you for saving my life, for giving me the chance to learn that Auguste... could have carried a very different meaning."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Love and hatred are a privilege of the living.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: When someone dies, their thoughts, feelings, and intentions die with them. In that sense, what Auguste truly represents in the language of flowers will forever remain a mystery.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But... even if it's only a conjecture, I would like to believe my own interpretation.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: The meaning we give to flowers, the symbolism we assign to our perfumes... They're constantly twisted and exploited in our imperfect world...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: And yet, at the very outset, they're born from the simplest and most beautiful desires we hold in our heart.

choices.text: Did you use the accord from back in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We need to hurry. Now is not the time to wander.)

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: How could something like that happen in broad daylight...

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: The shadow-like figure ran in the direction of the elevator, and my partner immediately chased after them...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...We should hurry, before they're forced to confront each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where in the world did he go... Oh, let's ask the merchants nearby!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The scent is getting stronger. This must be the place.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And thus, all the turmoil caused by "Auguste" finally comes to an end...\nA few weeks later, you receive a letter from Emilie inviting you to catch up in Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: This is terrifying...

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: No! Don't come any closer!
